subject: gk
question: Which of the following Amendment Acts laid down fundamental duties for Indian citizens?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The 42nd Amendment Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 added a new part called IV-A to the Indian Constitution, which is titled "Fundamental Duties".
 
• It introduced Article 51A, which outlines ten fundamental duties for Indian citizens.
 
• This amendment was enacted during the Emergency period by the Indira Gandhi government.
 
• The fundamental duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties:**

 
 
• They are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.
 
• They aim to remind citizens that while enjoying their rights, they should also be conscious of their duties towards the nation.
 
 
 
• **List of Fundamental Duties:**
 
 
• To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions.
 
• To cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom.
 
• To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• To defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so.
 
• To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act:**
 
 
• Also known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its wide-ranging changes.
 
• It gave primacy to the Directive Principles of State Policy over the Fundamental Rights.
 
• Extended the term of Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies from 5 to 6 years.
 
 
 
• **Non-Justiciable Nature:**
 
 
• Fundamental duties are moral obligations and are not enforceable by law.
 
• However, they serve as a constant reminder to citizens to act responsibly.
